content:
I asked 10 people a question I’ve been thinking about:

Which post changed everything for you? 

Not necessarily your most popular post, but the piece of content that ended up leading somewhere you never expected.

If you're wondering what to post, I think these answers are a great place to start.

Here's what they said: 

Mischa Collins

“The first two posts I wrote about losing my job massively exceeded my expectations.

I was SO nervous to post them because I felt like a total failure for losing my job and not being able to get another one.

But I think the rawness of them allowed people to really connect.

The second one went super viral and I signed 2 clients off the back of it. That was the pivotal moment in my career because that's when I started working for myself.”

Courtney Johnson 📣 Social Media

“I posted a content series on TikTok called ‘Problematic Career Cheat Codes.’ That series led to a book deal with the biggest publisher in the world.

It worked because it was the thing I was the most scared to post, therefore the most authentic.”

Alice Lemee

“I published my first article on Creator Gravity, a term I'd coin to describe when creators have a magnetic force around them that pulls in people and opportunities.

That post became so popular on Substack I turned it into a six-part newsletter series. That then evolved into gaining hundreds of Substack subscribers, being asked on podcasts to speak on it, and opening a 1:1 coaching service.

I think it worked because it gave language to something people had seen before but couldn't fully put into words.”


I love these answers because the thing that changed everything wasn’t the thing they expected.

It was the thing they were scared to say.

It was putting a name to something people already felt.

And sometimes you really don’t know what a piece of content is going to do until you put it out there.

I have more of these, so part 2 coming soon.
